items.title: Provider/model ownership and three-axis resolution are explicit
items.statement: Models_System is explicitly the provider/model selection SSOT, and it distinguishes candidate source, user request, and executed value while requiring requested/effective disclosure across execution scopes.
items.impact: This is a sound authority and propagation boundary for runtime snapshots, inspectors, worktrees, and delegated execution.

evidence.exact_quote: This document is the **single canonical source of truth** for the Puppet Master model selection, configuration, and variant system — how models are identified, selected, overridden per Persona, and cycled via variants. All other plan documents MUST reference this document by anchor (e.g., `Plans/Models_System.md#MODEL-ID`) rather than restating model selection rules or variant definitions.

Settings resolution is always described on three axes:
- `source`: where a candidate value came from (`manual_override`, `persona_preference`, `surface_default`, `scope_policy`, `config_default`, `provider_default`).
- `request`: the value explicitly requested for this run or child run.
- `execution`: the value actually handed to the selected provider/runtime after capability checks, worktree assignment, and policy gating.

items.title: Effort transforms are prose, not an executable mapping contract

items.title: Capability provenance and staleness are first-class
items.statement: The source requires capability snapshots to retain provider/model/runtime identity, source references, observation time, verification, and staleness, while keeping unknown and inferred states visible.
items.impact: This supports observability, stale-data disclosure, and route-specific capability audits.

evidence.exact_quote: Capability snapshot provenance is mandatory for context-window, max-token, and fallback fields. Each snapshot records `capability_snapshot_id`, `provider_entry_id`, `model_id`, `runtime_surface_id`, `source_refs[]`, `source_kind`, `observed_at_utc`, `verification_state`, and `staleness_state`. Unknown, opaque, stale, inferred, clamped, and unsupported states must remain visible rather than silently substituting a legacy default.

items.title: Context-limit field names diverge inside the owner contract
items.statement: The standard capability table uses *_tokens names, while overflow ownership switches to context_window and effective_context_window. No alias or migration rule says whether these are the same fields.
items.impact: Adapters, compaction, retry classification, and persisted snapshots can read different keys and lose overflow evidence.

evidence.exact_quote:
| `context_window_tokens` | integer | Provider/model advertised total context window for the concrete runtime surface |
| `max_input_tokens` | integer? | Maximum input budget when the provider distinguishes input from total context |
| `max_output_tokens` | integer? | Maximum output/generation budget for the concrete provider/model entry |
| `effective_context_window_tokens` | integer | Runtime-safe context limit after route, account, model variant, and policy clamps |
| `fallback_chain[]` | array | Ordered fallback candidates with rank, provider/model identity, eligibility, capability deltas, rejection reason, and selected marker |

Model overflow detection is a model/runtime capability question before it becomes a retry or compaction decision. The model capability snapshot owns `context_window`, `effective_context_window`, `max_input_tokens`, `max_output_tokens`, `supports_truncation_signal`, and provider-specific overflow signal evidence. An adapter or provider may report overflow, length truncation, context-window exhaustion, or equivalent status, but it must preserve the provider signal and requested/effective model snapshot instead of converting it into a generic retry reason. Prompt compaction and context assembly consume these fields through `Plans/Prompt_Pipeline.md#COMPACTION` and `#COMPACTION-THRESHOLDS`; runtime retry policy consumes the classified outcome after model overflow has been attributed.

items.impact: Concurrent dispatch and catalog refresh can produce invalid or unrecoverable lifecycle states.

evidence.exact_quote: Model catalog entries carry `model_lifecycle_state` with closed values `active | deprecated | sunset_pending | sunset | removed`. evidence.exact_quote:
Deterministic alias resolution requirements:
- Alias keys MUST be normalized by lowercasing and collapsing spaces/underscores/hyphens.
- Resolution order for user-provided model text is: alias → exact model id → exact display name.
- If no match is found, the caller receives a model-unavailable result from the requesting subsystem.

Implementations MUST ship these aliases in the default alias registry; users MAY add or override aliases in config. Overrides can affect lookup, not capability truth; provider/model support still comes from catalog metadata plus route-specific verification.

items.title: Fallback, retry, and attempt identity are correctly separated

evidence.exact_quote:
### Ownership split
- model selection decides requested/effective provider/model before execution begins
- runtime policy decides whether an attempt is retried, remediated, blocked, or escalated after a classified outcome
- providers and adapters may not invent model-local retry loops that bypass runtime policy

### Required attempt snapshots


Each attempt MUST retain requested and effective model/provider identifiers so users can later explain why a blocked or failed attempt ran under a specific effective configuration.

### Fallback rule
Model fallback may change the effective model only through the shared model-selection contract, never as an implicit side effect of provider transient handling inside an already-running attempt.

items.title: Dynamic catalogs and fallback chains have no scale or resource limits
items.statement: The source makes discovery dynamic and refreshable but defines no maximum catalog size, fallback-chain length, page/batch contract, refresh concurrency, timeout budget, memory bound, backpressure, or behavior for extremely large provider/model sets.
items.impact: Large or hostile catalogs can stall boot/refresh, exhaust memory, make pickers unusable, or create unbounded fallback evaluation.

evidence.exact_quote: Provider/catalog discovery remains dynamic and model-scoped. OpenCode `models.dev` and provider `/catalog` evidence may supply model-level capability metadata such as reasoning, `/tool/temperature` support, limits, modalities, and pricing; PM records this as capability data rather than hardcoding provider defaults. Selectable-unit snapshots preserve `requested_default` and `effective_capabilities` so UI defaults and runtime routing can explain which provider/model entry was requested and what capability block was actually discovered. `cursor-agent models` is live catalog evidence whose returned IDs may encode reasoning variants directly, so PM must discover those IDs instead of inferring variants from vendor name alone.

- model discovery `/state`, including whether stale cached models remain visible while refresh runs, whether a single provider refresh failed, and whether progress is partial or complete.
- explicit actions for `Refresh Models` and `Refresh Providers`; initial connect, reconnect, and app boot/profile activation may refresh automatically, but user-triggered refreshes stay visible and scoped.

items.title: MS-011 through MS-016 preserve useful presentation, identity, and option boundaries
items.statement: The final six core PlanUnits keep GUI presentation over canonical state, enforce first-slash model-ID grammar, separate runtime-platform evidence, retire Gemini CLI selection guidance, and establish provider-before-model option scope.
items.impact: These boundaries reduce display-driven identity drift and configuration-scope ambiguity.

canonical_text: Stored and runtime model IDs use provider_id/model_id, split only on the first slash, and cannot be rewritten

canonical_text: Selection follows the deterministic requested/effective pipeline and priority table. Concrete provider entries

principal_builder_blockers: Conflicting precedence chains prevent a single deterministic resolver.
The canonical alias table emits noncanonical bare model IDs.
Effort transforms and direct coding-plan routes lack executable matrices.
The canonical capability-snapshot example omits fields declared mandatory.
Refresh, lifecycle, and destructive crew transitions lack concurrency and rollback contracts.
PlanUnit acceptance criteria prove migration shape, not the behavior each unit specifies.
strong_explicit_boundaries: Catalog presence is not support proof and generated-media rows remain evidence-gated.
Fallback selection is separate from retry and new attempts retain requested/effective snapshots.
Provider capability is separate from primary/fallback routing posture.
Canonical stored identity is intended to remain separate from GUI labels and runtime-platform context.
